name: John R. Furner

career.title: Hourly associate, then store, district, buying, regional and sourcing roles (incl. VP of Global Sourcing)
Executive Vice President and Chief Merchandising Officer

background_rationale: Spent his entire 30+ year career inside Walmart, rising from hourly store associate through store operations, merchandising and sourcing to run Sam's Club and Walmart U.S.

notable.summary: As incoming CEO, announced an executive reorganization effective Feb. 1, 2026, naming new heads of Walmart U.S., Walmart International and Sam's Club U.S. and creating a Chief Growth Officer role, citing AI reshaping retail.

On his first earnings call as CEO, Furner said Walmart's use of technology and AI was helping reduce friction and simplify decision-making, as the company reported fiscal 2026 revenue of about $713 billion.
Walmart laid off or relocated about 1,000 corporate employees, mainly in global technology and AI product teams, as part of a restructuring to streamline teams.
In a public letter to customers, Furner pledged that Walmart will not use customer data or AI to set personalized prices, stating "We price the product, not the person."

open_issues: Start year of Walmart China role unconfirmed: AndNowUKnow implies ~2013-2015 (two years before Oct 2015), Wikipedia suggests ~2014-2017; start left null.
Graduation year 1996 sourced only from Wikipedia; Walmart's official bio gives no year.
Date of the personalized-pricing letter: Shelby Report says Sept 25, 2026, Fox Business reports Sept 27; recorded as 2026-09.

Father's Walmart tenure differs: NWA Democrat-Gazette (2018) says 21 years (assistant regional manager to regional VP); Fortune (Mar 2026) says 25 years, joining operations in 1977. Story says only 'regional manager'.

Mother's illness timing differs: NWA says diagnosed 1988, died April 1989; Fortune says she fell ill in 1987 and store managers raised money for the family (story not clearly attributed to Furner, so omitted).

First job location: Walmart bio and Fortune say Store 100 garden center (1993); NWA 2018 profile describes a part-time start at Sam's Club and work at a Springdale Walmart during college. Order/timing of the Mexico internship relative to 1993 is unclear.

personal_story.hook: John Furner started at Walmart stacking mulch in a store garden center; 33 years later, he runs the company.
personal_story.summary: Furner grew up in central Arkansas, the son of a Walmart regional manager, and spent summers on his grandfather's farm gathering eggs and selling watermelons at a roadside stand. He lost his mother when he was 14, and says that to understand who he is, you'd have to have met her. As a teenager he got hooked on a $125 guitar, and at the University of Arkansas he played in a cover band for a few months and switched majors several times before settling on marketing. In 1993 he took a part-time hourly job in the garden center of Walmart's Store 100 in Bentonville, and an internship at a Sam's Club in Mexico showed him shopping as a family outing. From there he worked through store, buying and international roles to lead Sam's Club, then Walmart U.S., and, from February 2026, all of Walmart.

quote.text: If you wanted to know the reason I am who I am, you'd have to meet my mom.
quote.context: Interview with the Northwest Arkansas Democrat-Gazette 'High Profile' column, Feb. 2018, while Sam's Club CEO
